message.reasoning: We need to answer the question: "SSO vs password, both at once?" The user likely asks if they can have both SSO and password sign-in at the same time. According to policy excerpts: Enabling SSO does not immediately disable password sign-in for existing staff. Both methods coexist until an admin separately turns password sign-in off, in Settings → Security → SSO → Require SSO. So answer: Yes, both can be used until you enable Require SSO. Provide that info. Also mention that once Require SSO is enabled, password sign-in is turned off. So answer accordingly.

function.arguments: {"message":"Yes – when you first enable SSO, existing staff can still log in with their passwords. Both methods coexist until you go to Settings → Security → SSO and turn on “Require SSO.” Once that’s enabled, password sign‑in is disabled for the whole workspace."}

arguments.message: Yes – when you first enable SSO, existing staff can still log in with their passwords. Both methods coexist until you go to Settings → Security → SSO and turn on “Require SSO.” Once that’s enabled, password sign‑in is disabled for the whole workspace.
